target_customer: Engineering and data platform teams running event driven and streaming data systems such as Kafka and RabbitMQ
problem: Teams could not easily see, repair or replay bad data flowing through streaming systems, and usually built custom in house tooling for it.
business_model: open source core with a SaaS platform for data observability and in flight data handling
product_category: Streaming data observability and data quality

founders.name: Ustin Zarubin
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch says both founders worked at New Relic, InVision, DigitalOcean and Community.com; YC lists physics and distributed systems interests for Zarubin.

founders.name: Daniel Selans
founders.background_notes: Data pipelines and high throughput systems.

exit.reason: The archived snitch repository README says the company was acquired for an undisclosed amount to an acquirer under NDA, and that founders and engineers moved on. YC lists Inactive.

technical_complexity.rationale: Inspecting, transforming and replaying encoded messages across brokers at high throughput, with schema handling and PII detection, is hard systems work for a small team in 2020.

defensibility.rationale: Open source clients and a thin SaaS layer on top of commodity brokers were easy to replace, and the main alternative was in house tooling.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not established from dated sources; broker vendors and observability vendors added streaming monitoring features over time.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in 2023 quoted the founder saying the main competitor was in house engineering teams building custom fixes, and that customers such as Recharge and ParkMobile paid. The open source tool Plumber reportedly had over 150,000 downloads.

rebrands.why: The seed round announcement said funds would help with a rebrand from Batch to Streamdal; reason not stated.

branding.community_and_virality: Open source repositories and a Discord server; Product Hunt listing. No evidence of merch or press about the brand itself.

brand_strength.rationale: Little evidence of recognition beyond a small developer community; the rebrand came late and the company later went inactive.

pivots.from: Batch, data replay and observability for message queues
pivots.to: Streamdal, observing, repairing and replaying data in streaming systems, later code native data pipelines
pivots.why: Not sourced; the rename was announced with the seed round, and the 2024 site calls it an open source platform for code native data pipelines.

outcome_analysis: Streamdal raised a 5.4 million dollar seed led by Work-Bench in 2022, announced in February 2023, and reported 7.2 million raised in total plus named paying customers. YC now lists it as Inactive, and an archived repository README says it was acquired by an unnamed buyer under NDA with the team moving on. No post-mortem or press report states the cause, so the cause is not public and failure factors are left empty.
notes: Status conflict: YC says Inactive, the repo README says acquired; exit type left unknown because the acquisition rests on one self reported source. Seed date from a third party copy of the About page (Sept 2022); public announcement 2023-02-08. TechCrunch says 7.2M total raised, so about 1.8M of earlier funding (likely YC and others) is unitemized. An aggregator (loot-drop.io) claims 7.0M burned and a 2023 end year; unverified and ignored. Competitor search found only undated Kafka tool roundups, so the competitor list is empty; the founder named in house teams as the main competitor in 2023.
